messages.content: You are a helpful assistant. You give concise, practical answers.

I told a friend I couldn't make her birthday because of work, but actually I
just didn't want to go. She's now offered to move it. What do I say?

Keep it honest, kind, and clear. Avoid doubling down on the work excuse, and don't leave the ball in her court.

**If you want to keep the friendship but skip the party:**
> "Thanks so much for offering to move it—I really appreciate you thinking of me. To be honest, I've realized I just need some downtime right now and won't be able to commit to a celebration, even on a new date. I hope you understand, and I really hope you have a wonderful birthday anyway."

**If you want to stay connected without making plans:**
Add: *"I'd love to grab coffee or lunch with you sometime in the next few weeks just to catch up."*

**Why this works:**
- Closes the loop on the work excuse without lying further
- Gives a firm, respectful "no" so she can actually celebrate
- Leaves the relationship intact on your terms

Pick the version that matches whether you want to see her later or just step back gently. Then send it and move on.
ugh yeah but like what exact words? do i text it or call

**Text it.** It gives you both space, avoids real-time pressure, and is completely appropriate for declining plans.

Pick the exact version that matches what you want:

**Option 1: Clean & direct (no follow-up plans)**
> "Hey [Name], thank you so much for offering to move it. I really appreciate you thinking of me. To be honest, I’ve realized I just need some quiet time right now and won’t be able to make a celebration work, even on a new date. I hope you understand, and I really hope you have a fantastic birthday!"

**Option 2: Declines the party, keeps the friendship warm**
> "Hi [Name], thanks for offering to reschedule. I’ve realized I’m just in a headspace where I need to keep things really low-key lately, so I won’t be able to commit to a birthday celebration. I’d still love to grab coffee or lunch with you in the next couple weeks just to catch up, though. Wishing you the best on your birthday!"

**Option 3: Short & firm**
> "Hey [Name], I really appreciate you offering to move it. I’ve realized I just need some personal downtime right now and won’t be able to make it work on another date either. Thanks for understanding, and I hope you have a wonderful birthday!"

**Send it as-is.** Don't over-explain, don't apologize more than once, and don't wait for a reply to feel relieved. She'll get the message, and you'll avoid the awkwardness of a phone call or a second round of scheduling.
thanks. sent option 3. she replied "oh that's totally fine! hope everything's ok 💕" ...do i just like it or respond

**Like it.** A quick reaction (❤️, 👍, or 😊) is perfectly appropriate here. It acknowledges her message, closes the loop politely, and doesn't invite more back-and-forth.

If you prefer to send a short text instead:
> "Thanks, I really appreciate it! Have the best birthday 💛"

Either way, let it rest. She accepted gracefully, so no further explanation is needed. You handled it cleanly.
